**Bank of England sets design direction for UK retail payments overhaul**

*A layered architecture built on ISO 20022, settling in central bank money and supporting payment types from account-to-account at point of sale to agentic payments, will form the blueprint for the system that replaces Faster Payments and Bacs.*

The Bank of England has outlined prospective design proposals for the next-generation retail payments infrastructure that will succeed the clearing and messaging layers behind Faster Payments and Bacs. The Retail Payments Infrastructure Board (RPIB), chaired by the Bank, published its response to a June consultation on November 4, drawing on 121 submissions from banks, fintechs, infrastructure providers, merchants and consumer groups.

Respondents broadly supported the proposed direction, including a single modular architecture, settlement in central bank money and a phased migration that manages disruption across the wider ecosystem. Some questioned whether alternatives to central bank money settlement should be available for blockchain-based payments and whether all retail transactions, including certain tokenised deposits, would need to clear through the new infrastructure. The Bank indicated that most product-level arrangements could continue to settle on a prefunded net basis, with more frequent settlement cycles now technically feasible following its real-time gross settlement renewal programme.

The response also confirmed that the infrastructure should support new payment types identified by respondents, including account-to-account payments at point of sale, payments between different forms of money, alias-based instant payments, agentic payments and embedded finance. Co-creation work between the Bank and industry began this month, with the RPIB due to hand over a completed blueprint to an industry-owned delivery company in spring 2027.

*Sources: [Response to the RPIB consultation on the Design of the Future Retail Payments Infrastructure](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/paper/2026/cp/response-to-the-rpib-consultation) — Bank of England*

**Klarna prepares XS2A v2 to replace its legacy open banking API**

*The rebuilt API signals a shift from compliance-driven open banking infrastructure toward a platform designed for commercial scale and reliability.*

Klarna is preparing the second version of its XS2A open banking API, which will replace the legacy interface that has underpinned its account information and payment initiation services across Europe. The new API is designed to address long-standing reliability and developer experience shortcomings in the original platform.

Klarna's open banking infrastructure, which originated from its 2014 acquisition of SOFORT and was later consolidated under its Kosma unit launched in March 2022, serves as the connectivity layer for third parties accessing bank data and initiating payments. The original XS2A API was built primarily to meet PSD2 compliance obligations, and its architecture reflects that origin. A ground-up rebuild suggests Klarna sees open banking connectivity as a commercial product line, not merely a regulatory obligation.

The timing aligns with broader industry moves to professionalise open banking infrastructure ahead of PSD3. As the European Commission prepares to extend data-sharing obligations and tighten API performance standards, providers with modern, scalable interfaces will be better positioned to compete for both fintech and bank clients.

*Sources: [Klarna prepares XS2A v2 to replace its legacy open banking API](https://thepaypers.com/fintech/news/klarna-prepares-xs2a-v2-to-replace-its-legacy-open-banking-api) — The Paypers*

**Mastercard integrates open finance data into mortgage lending via Tidalwave**

*The partnership extends open finance capabilities into the mortgage origination process, where permissioned bank data could displace manual income verification.*

Mastercard is integrating its open finance data capabilities into Tidalwave's mortgage platform, giving lenders access to permissioned consumer financial data during the origination process. The partnership is aimed at replacing manual document-based income and expenditure checks with real-time bank data.

Mortgage lending has been slower than consumer credit to adopt open banking data, partly because of the higher regulatory burden around affordability assessments and partly because the existing broker-led process is deeply entrenched. The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) published a consultation on mortgage lending rule reforms on June 9, and a separate open finance policy sprint the same week explored how bank data could support affordability checks, but lender adoption has remained limited.

The payments company has been building its open finance business as a distinct commercial line since its acquisition of Finicity, and this partnership extends that strategy into one of the largest consumer lending segments. The move follows the open finance taskforce of the FCA identifying mortgage origination as a priority use case, and positions Mastercard alongside credit reference agencies as a data intermediary in the underwriting chain.

*Sources: [Mastercard, Tidalwave bring Open Finance to mortgages](https://thepaypers.com/fintech/news/mastercard-and-tidalwave-partner-on-open-finance-for-mortgage-lenders) — The Paypers*

stories.original:
**Bottomline adds stablecoin payments to its corporate treasury platform**

*USDC-based cross-border payments through an established corporate treasury platform mark a step toward stablecoin normalisation in mainstream B2B payment workflows.*

Bottomline has completed cross-border stablecoin payments through its Global Payments Hub and Cash Management platform using Circle's USDC. The integration allows corporate treasury teams to initiate and settle cross-border payments in stablecoins alongside conventional fiat rails within the same platform.

The distribution channel matters more here than the technology. Bottomline's platform is used by banks and corporates for high-volume payment processing, and embedding stablecoin settlement within that workflow removes the need for separate crypto-native infrastructure. It follows a pattern that has emerged across the payments industry over the past year, where established platforms such as Mastercard and Visa have added stablecoin settlement options to existing merchant and bank networks.

Settlement speed and cost on specific corridors where correspondent banking remains slow and expensive provide the practical appeal. Whether adoption follows will depend on counterparty willingness to receive stablecoin-denominated payments and on the regulatory treatment of USDC in recipient jurisdictions, particularly after its designation as the EU's first significant e-money token under MiCA.

*Sources: [Bottomline brings USDC stablecoin payments into platform](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/111632/bottomline-brings-usdc-stablecoin-payments-into-platform?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
